title: Hosted API capacity contingency matrix by region (Q4 2026)
content:
Executive summary:
This worksheet captures projected peak traffic for the Redwood hosted API for Q4 2026 broken down by region, model-family, and GPU pool. The goal is to define a contingency matrix (safety pools + dynamic reserve) expressed as tokens/sec and QPS, with clear operational levers to avoid customer-facing throttles during multi-region spikes or GPU pool failures.

Key goals:
- Provide a 99th-percentile operational buffer expressed as both tokens/sec and equivalent QPS by model family and region.
- Quantify the minimal prewarm reservation (in racks/GPU slices) required to meet 95% of modeled spike scenarios within 30s.
- Enumerate fallback routing policies and owners for capacity escalations.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Traffic mix: 60% conversational chat (average 120 tokens per response), 30% completion-style (avg 25 tokens), 10% embeddings/short calls.
- Model distribution: 45% redwood-v2-medium (8B eq), 30% community-30b (quantized variant), 25% instruction-large (60B).
- GPU families in fleet: H100-80GB (primary), A100-80GB (secondary), L40S (burst/backfill).
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (baseline): H100=85k t/s, A100=48k t/s, L40S=30k t/s (these are steady-state during mixed-length workloads).
- Average session QPS mapping: tokens/sec -> QPS depends on model and response length; we use a conversion table below.

Conversion table (examples):
- redwood-v2-medium: 120 tokens/response -> 10 responses/sec per 1k tokens/sec -> 8 QPS per 1k tokens/sec (rounded for planning)
- community-30b: 120 tokens/response -> 10 responses/sec per 1k tokens/sec -> 8 QPS per 1k tokens/sec
- instruction-large: 120 tokens/response -> 10 responses/sec per 1k tokens/sec -> 8 QPS per 1k tokens/sec
(For short calls/completions scale proportionally).

Projected peak (conservative scenario, 2026-11-15 simulated peak):
- North America (NA): peak tokens/sec demand = 4,200,000 t/s (mixed models). Safety buffer target = +18% => contingency = 756,000 t/s. Total planning capacity target = 4,956,000 t/s.
- Europe (EU): peak tokens/sec demand = 1,600,000 t/s. Safety buffer target = +22% => contingency = 352,000 t/s. Planning capacity target = 1,952,000 t/s.
- APAC (AP): peak tokens/sec demand = 900,000 t/s. Safety buffer target = +30% => contingency = 270,000 t/s. Planning capacity target = 1,170,000 t/s.

Mapping to GPU slices (rough):
- NA target capacity 4.956M t/s -> H100 equivalent slices = 4,956,000 / 85,000 ≈ 59 H100 GPUs (baseline). With A100 fallbacks and heterogenous mix, plan for 75 GPU-equivalents across H100/A100/L40S.
- EU target capacity 1.952M t/s -> ≈ 23 H100 GPUs -> plan 30 GPU-equivalents.
- AP target capacity 1.170M t/s -> ≈ 14 H100 GPUs -> plan 19 GPU-equivalents.
Notes: "GPU-equivalents" means aggregated capacity normalized to H100 baseline; actual allocation will be a mix based on availability and cost.

Prewarm and reserve policy (operational levers):
1) Static prewarm pool: maintain minimum reserved pool sized to cover 60% of single-region sudden spikes for SLA-tier customers. For NA that equals ~2,520,000 t/s -> reserve ~30 H100-equivalent GPUs.
2) Dynamic reserve: elastic reserve of additional GPU-equivalents deployed via autoscale warmup (aim to reach target in 25-40s). Heat-up policy: spin up 8 GPU-equivalents per 15s per region until reached.
3) Cross-region failover: if NA suffers pool failure >15% capacity for >60s, route a subset of non-latency-critical traffic to EU with explicit cost tagging and model downscaling (quantized variants).

Contingency matrix (scenarios):
- Scenario A (single data-center outage in NA): expected shortfall = 20–35% -> rely on static prewarm + cross-region routing + temporary rate-limits on free-tier; owner: infra-oncall.
- Scenario B (global traffic surge + supply constraints): expected shortfall if no bursting = 40–60% -> activate emergency procurement pool (spot/HPC) + degrade model choice to quantized 30b -> owner: capacity-runway lead.
- Scenario C (GPU kernel regression causing 10% throughput drop): immediate mitigation = toggle kernel fallback + increase static prewarm via manual override; owner: serving-runtime oncall.

Quantified runbook snippets (for playbook inclusion):
- If observed tokens/sec > planned + buffer for 3 consecutive 10s windows, page infra-runway and trigger dynamic reserve expansion.
- If prewarm fill < 70% after 30s of scale event, mark incident Sev2 and shift non-critical workloads off primary pool.

Open risks and unknowns:
- Model mix shifts: adoption of a new 65B family would change tokens-per-sec efficiency assumptions materially; re-run the model profiler before finalizing Q4 procurement.
- Cloud region procurement lead times and quota approvals for H100s in APAC may be >21 days.
- Cost vs latency tradeoffs: higher safety buffers in APAC driven by regional variability increase unit-cost by ~12% in projected run-rate.

Next actions (owners):
- Maya Patel: run per-model microbenchmarks for community-30b quantized variant across H100/A100 by 2026-03-12.
- Daniel Kim: validate spot bursting timeline and autoscaler warmup rates in staging by 2026-03-08.
- Owen Li: draft a short customer-facing note describing contingency routing and expected impact on SLAs for enterprise customers (due 2026-03-15).

Appendix: sample calculation (NA):
- Baseline demand = 4.2M t/s. Buffer = 18% -> 4.2M * 1.18 = 4,956,000 t/s target.
- H100-equivalents = ceil(4,956,000 / 85,000) = 59 -> add 25% for heterogeneity/ops margin -> 59 * 1.25 = 74 -> round to 75 GPU-equivalents.

Spreadsheet layout (sheet names / ranges referenced for engineers):
- Sheet 'Inputs' A1:A12 = assumptions; B1:B12 = values.
- Sheet 'ByRegion' row-per-region includes projected_peak, buffer_pct, contingency_tokens, target_capacity, gpu_equiv.
- Sheet 'Runbook' enumerates playbook steps with owners and run thresholds.

If this looks reasonable, I'll convert the sheet into a shared Google Sheet (link in linked_artifacts) and schedule a 30-minute sync with infra + serving-runtime next week to finalize warmup timings and procurement ask.
